messages:
lin: Proposal: 'adaptive-threshold' gate for new v3q bring-up. Instead of fixed global thresholds, compute slice-aware baselines and allow dynamic threshold multipliers based on sample size and historical volatility.

omar: interesting. so thresholds loosen on noisy slices and tighten on stable ones?

lin: exactly. formula sketch: effective_threshold = baseline + k * historical_std_dev / sqrt(n_samples). k defaults to 1.6 for 95% safety.

riyad: that helps avoid false positives on tiny slices. what's the auto-fallback rule?

lin: fallback if: (1) weighted aggregate breach > global_limit AND (2) two independent signals (mrr_drop OR fidelity_drop) exceed their adaptive thresholds OR p99_latency > hard_limit.

ops-bot: note: we should surface "breach_reason_vector" and the slice-level baseline in telemetry for postmortem.

omar: can we combine with a staged cutover? i.e., start at 1% -> 5% -> 20% with re-eval at each step using the adaptive gate.

lin: yes. staged_cutover: [1,5,20,100] percents with a minimum dwell time and minimum sample floor. If an intermediate step trips the gate, auto-roll back to previous safe step and open a human review ticket.

riyad: secondary idea: during stage steps allow a short "quiet shadow" of the downstream reranker to detect regressions unseen in MRR. This catches quality regressions that aggregate metrics miss.

lin: add as optional step. good call. we'll call it "shadow-compare" and compute concordance score on a held slice.

eval-bot: quick simulation results for model=v3q-candidate run_sim=1776:
```
samples: total=18k, slices={faq:30%, long-form:25%, multi-turn:25%, misc:20%}
baseline_mrr: 0.287, candidate_mrr: 0.279 -> mrr_drop=-0.028
slice_stats:
  long-form: drop=-0.055, std=0.018, n=4500
  multi-turn: drop=-0.012, std=0.010, n=4500
  faq: drop=-0.001, std=0.006, n=5400
  misc: drop=-0.009, std=0.014, n=3600
adaptive_thresholds:
  long-form: -0.034 (baseline + k*std/sqrt(n))
  multi-turn: -0.020
decision: weighted_aggregate_breach=true, independent_signal_count=2 -> automatic downgrade to previous version at 5% traffic
```

lin: so sim predicted auto-downgrade at stage 5%. We should run a focused eval on long-form slice to understand prompts driving drop.

omar: also check quantization bits mapping; v3q used int4 mix with asymmetric per-layer mapping vs baseline quant config. Could be head-layer sensitivity.

riyad: ops note: make sure the rollback creates a trace event and tags the model hash + quant-config so we can diff.

release-owner: I'll own the human review if automatic rollback occurs. Can we add an expedited noisy-slice re-run step that reruns 10k long-form prompts with golden annotations?

lin: yep add to playbook: "expedited_local_eval": run 10k long-form with annotations, run fidelity, hallucination checks, and token-level alignment. If results improve, we can allow a soft-retry with stricter dwell times.

eval-bot: follow-up A/B split actual run id=1776a deployed to 5% for 40m:
reports:
  aggregate mrr_drop: -0.026
  long-form drop: -0.052 (weighted 25%)
  p99_latency: +8ms (within hard limit)
decision: adaptive_gate -> long-form breach exceeds adaptive threshold, independent signals=2 -> triggered rollback to baseline at previous step (1%) and created ticket TKT-4832 for triage.

omar: triage plan: (1) repro on annotated long prompts, (2) inspect per-layer activation shifts, (3) run alternate quant config int4v2 and int8 fallback.

lin: minor change: until triage complete, pin model routing to baseline for 95% traffic and keep candidate in shadow at 5% for concordance checks.

ops-bot: rollback event logged. tags: model:candidate-v3q, quant:int4-mixed, reason_vector:[long-form,fidelity], rollback_trigger=adaptive_gate

riyad: action owners: lin (eval), omar (quant debug), release-owner (human triage). ETA initial findings in 24h.

lin: adding gatebook entry draft: "adaptive-threshold-staggered-cutover" with formula, staged steps, soft shadow-compare, and expedited eval playbook.

release-owner: acked. tagging product and platform leads for visibility.

lin: thanks. we'll re-run after quant config tweaks and post results here.

eval-bot: snapshot t+24h: candidate with int4v2 mapping reduced long-form drop to -0.018 in re-run; adaptive gate would have allowed progress to 20% but still recommend focused hallucination checks before full promote.

lin: excellent. closing this thread once PRs go green and gatebook entry merged.
